name: P ZERO Race TLR RS

origin.basis: Italian tire maker; Pirelli says the P ZERO Race range is made at its plant in Italy near its Milan headquarters.

manufacturing.basis: Pirelli: the P ZERO Race range is made in Italy (Bollate factory).

positioning: Pirelli's top SpeedCORE race tire developed with World Tour teams, with the SmartEVO2 compound.
pressure_note: The product page gives no maximum pressure; use the figure printed on the tire.

wet_notes.summary: Pirelli claims SmartEVO2 improves grip and handling on dry and especially wet surfaces.

availability.note: Listed in Pirelli's UK catalogue with a dealer finder; sold by retail shops on Tmall and Taobao in mainland China (no official Pirelli store found) and stocked by a US retailer on 2026-11-01.

price_observations.market: 宝祥丰运动户外专营店 (Tmall retailer)
price_observations.conditions: Retail shop list price before discounts on 2026-11-01 for the unboxed black 30C option; coupon price CNY 419.8. Not an official Pirelli store; single or pair not stated.
Retailer price on 2026-11-01 for the 28 mm black tire with local stock; the page does not state one tire or a pair.

caveats: Race casing: lower tread puncture score than the standard P ZERO Race TLR in the same lab.
Hookless compatibility and maximum pressure are not stated on the product page.
Mainland China price is from a retail shop, not an official Pirelli store.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other. The Classic, Retro and team colour editions count as the same tire.

reports.summary: Runs perfectly on the road once a shop fitted it to rims it did not suit well.
Grips well in the dry and wet and seems to roll really well.
Feels fast; soft enough that the owner would keep it for summer racing.
Superb once on: confidence-inspiring in all conditions so far, with GP5000 speed and a supple ride, though the first pair was far too tight.
Slightly less supple than the owner's previous Vittorias and so hard to fit that a shop had to do it, a worry for roadside repairs.
Two front sidewall failures, bulges on two tires and a rear puncture in five months; the owner now advises an insert in the front.
Excellent so far in 28 mm tubeless: fast, grippy, comfortable and reasonably robust for a race tire, and easier to mount than the GP5000 S TR.
Fast and grippy with no puncture so far; mounting was a struggle and the tires stretch after a few hundred miles.
On the owner's home city roads they punctured constantly, needed several plugs and had next to no wet grip; on smooth roads abroad they felt ultra fast.
Highly recommended after about a month.
Very good grip with good comfort and rolling for ultra-distance riding, after a painful installation.
One slide in the wet and a puncture that needed a plug in 1,200 km; the owner's confidence is gone.
A puncture that sealant would not close; the first plug broke and the owner rode home at low pressure.
The team edition feels noticeably faster than the standard P ZERO Race TLR.
Perhaps the best tubeless tires the owner has used for balancing speed, protection and ride feel; very hard to mount on new wheels.
Raised the owner's average speed on a hilly morning loop by over 1 mph against the older non-RS version, and has handled bad roads for weeks.
Two tires punctured so badly early on that they were plugged and retired; the next 30/32 mm pair has two sealed cuts after 500 km.
Amazing tires with better ride quality and more wet grip than the GP5000 S TR, though nearly impossible to mount.
Went back to the RS after the SL-R punctured three times in one ride, finding the RS better balanced.
Switched from the GP5000 S TR in 32 mm: the small rolling-resistance penalty is worth the better puncture protection and slower wear; very hard to mount.
